title: Write it on the sofa: fill the Paragraph's three slots, then OK reads it
body:
## Summary
Essay Master only helps once a paragraph exists; the family's real evening starts from a blank page ('Later school starts - first draft'). Add the plan: from the lens home, OK on 'Start from the pattern' opens the Paragraph play's three slots - your claim, the evidence, the link back - hatched on the TV. The learner says or types one sentence per slot on the phone; each slot inks with their own words; when all three are written, OK on the TV reads the paragraph through the chosen lens and lands on the forensic page.

## Description
Today the playbook teaches the pattern and dead-ends (keys.ts:366,369), and the home's 'Nothing read' card cannot be focused (EssayTV.tsx:176-184, keys.ts:110). The data and rules are already there: the slots are in the pattern (lessons.data.ts:51), the role guess is in code (rules/essay.ts:33), the one-sentence checks are revise()'s (rules/essay.ts:170-184), and the TV can start a reading itself (keys.ts:183 pattern, api/analyse kind essay). New pure functions in rules/essay: planSlots(play) derives the slots from the pattern; planFill refuses a blank, two sentences, a leftover [bracket] or an over-long text; planFit returns a code comment when the sentence's first-pass role does not match the slot (comment only - the slot inks because it is written, per FAMILY-PHASE-1-PLAN.md:49); planText joins the learner's sentences and proves they split back into three. Session: Screen 'essayplan', optional essayPlan {lens, slots: string[]} on Session and MathsSlot, events essay.plan (open, from the TV) and essay.slot (from the phone, validated in the reducer). TV (Specimen, no restyle): three rows - slot label in the pattern's 44 px words, a hatched plate with the caret on the focused one, the learner's sentence at 54 once written with a role arrow; the caption carries planFit's line or 'Say it on the phone'; actions Write on my phone / Read it / Back. Phone: on essayplan the Essay tab shows 'Slot 2 - the evidence', a textarea, Dictate and Send.

## Flow
- Lens home: Up/Down to a lens, Right to the card, Down to 'Start from the pattern', OK
- TV: three hatched slots, caret on 'Your claim'; phone's Essay tab follows (panelFor)
- Child dictates a sentence, Send -> slot inks with their words, caret moves on; a role mismatch is a caption, not a block
- Up/Down revisit a slot; Send again replaces it
- All written: OK on Read it -> /api/analyse kind essay -> the forensic page, as any reading

## Expected impact
The module becomes useful at the moment the homework is set, not only after a draft exists: blank page to a read paragraph in about five presses and three spoken sentences, with the parent watching the slots fill on the TV. No model call until Read it; nothing on screen the learner did not write (the frame words are never put into their text); the TV never asks for typing. Gate direction: plan slots are named in the Phase 1 plan as deferred, inside Essay Master's scope.

## Evaluation
Claim: from a blank page, the desk takes the learner through claim, evidence and link in their own sentences and reads the result, with every check in rules/essay.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass; 0 desk paths lead from the pattern to the learner's own paragraph (x-ray handles 2 keys, both leave)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first (node:test suites under tools/, no live model call)
Result: better
Gate: direction

title: A slip is set again on purpose, and rubbed out of the ruler when it stops
body:
## Summary
Math Buddy keeps a learner's slips as an append-only list of ids and never acts on them for the 12 school units it writes itself. Make the slip a tracked thing in code: Six more on a school unit is drawn so the learner's own slips would show and be named, and a slip the child stops making is rubbed out of the record, so its pencil scratch leaves the ruler.

## Description
The seam: the decision 'which questions expose this child's mistake' sits in two prompt sentences (items.ts:71, :219) for the model-written roads and nowhere at all for the code-written school units, although the Sheet tells the family every Six more is 'aimed at the slips the desk has seen' (MathsTV.tsx:794). Meanwhile school.ts already knows, exactly, the value each of 46 slips gives on any spec (slipCandidates, plus checkRatio's pairs) and uses it only to reject bad specs. And the record can only grow: learners.ts:289 appends, nothing removes, and the ruler draws the four oldest scratches forever (MathsTV.tsx:300).

The move, all in code: (1) school.ts exports slipShows(spec, slip) and slipValue(spec, slip), pinned against check() itself so 'shows' always means 'check would name it'. (2) makeSchoolItems takes an aim (the learner's live slips on the unit, newest first) and draws at least three of six items where an aimed slip shows, within the set's tier mix, still six distinct, still no model call; no aim is byte-identical to today. (3) Each attempt on a school item carries the slips its spec shows; rules/slips.ts (pure) decides the lifecycle: three usual right answers on items that show a slip since it was last made rub it out; making it again resets the count. learners.ts applies it and keeps a small held count per live slip. Step-up attempts and linear/Calculus slips are untouched (GUARD). (4) The ruler draws the newest four live slips; the Six more card says truthfully what it aims at.

Cost counted: 12 learner-blind generators, 46 slips with code-computable exposure, 1 TV claim that is false on 12 of 15 school topics, 2 prompt-only aims, 0 removal paths, and a measured baseline where a random six on dec-arith shows dec-lined-up three times in 0 of 100 sets.

## Flow
- Sheet: item 3 ringed 'Subtracted the wrong way round' -> marking records the slip.
- Six more (keys.ts:412 -> /api/practice -> makeItems -> makeSchoolItems with aim) -> six questions, at least three where that slip would show; the card names it in one line.
- The child gets those right -> each right attempt counts toward the slip's hold -> on the third, the slip leaves skills.slips and its scratch leaves the ruler on Tonight and Topics.
- The child slips again -> the count resets, the scratch stays.

## Expected impact
The family sees a specific mistake come back on purpose and then disappear from the ruler when it is beaten: progress as a picture, not a number. The Sheet's promise becomes true for the 12 code-written units, and the decision moves from a prompt into lib/rules. It also unlocks a parent line on the Sunday page ('stopped adding tops and bottoms') in a later card, with no model.

## Evaluation
Claim: school sets aim at the learner's own slips in code, and a beaten slip leaves the record and the ruler.
Before: 0 of 7 behaviour cases pass (case 7 is a declared GUARD); measured: dec-lined-up shows 3+ times in 0 of 100 random dec-arith sets, conv-top-dot-bottom in 15 of 100, wrong-direction in 51 of 100; slips are never removed.
After: 7 of 7 and the guard green; school-practice, school-stretch, school-marking, school-rules, maths-tv, maths-ruler, tv-sheet suites unchanged and green.
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: direction (rubbing a scratch out is not named in the context map or DESIGN-MATH-BUDDY.md; inside the module's scope: the ruler's slips and Six more). It is also an additive contract change to persisted learners.json (SkillRecord gains an optional held count). Consumers of SkillRecord.slips/held: learners.ts (cleanSkills, step, recordAttempt), items.ts (makeItems, the two prompt roads read slips unchanged), kinds.ts and mark.ts and explain.ts (attempt shows), MathsTV.tsx (ruler), the session's hydrated skills (store.ts REHYDRATE, not edited). Avoids the hot files store.ts, screens.tsx and keys.ts.
evidence: Probe (in-memory transpile of school.ts with slipCandidates/read/eq exported, seeds 0..199 x tiers 1-2 per unit): reachable 43 of 46; zero: ratio-share ratio-split-each 0, ratio-as-amounts 0, ratio-by-difference 0 (checkRatio pairs). Single-tier slips: frac-mul-div kept-second t1 0/t2 400, flipped-first t1 0/t2 400; dec-arith dec-lined-up t1 159/t2 0, dec-point-product t1 0/t2 400; area area-one-part t1 0/t2 132; ratio-swapped t1 30/t2 0. Baseline makeSchoolItems(unit, 6, k*7919), k=0..99, sets with >=3 items showing the slip: dec-arith dec-lined-up 0/100 (mean 1.10); dec-convert conv-top-dot-bottom 15/100 (1.25); frac-add-sub wrong-direction 51/100 (2.45); area area-no-half 50/100 (2.50); frac-add-sub tops-and-bottoms 100/100 (5.67). grep '\.slips\b' desk/src: items.ts:135, items.ts:283, learners.ts:181, learners.ts:289, MathsTV.tsx:300 - no removal. items.ts:332 signature: makeSchoolItems(topicId: string, n = 6, seed: number = freshSeed(), mix: Mix = "standard", stretch = false). MathsTV.tsx:794: `Six new questions on ${name}, aimed at the slips the desk has seen.`

title: Six like this one: a homework problem's unit, practised in one press
body:
## Summary
On homework night Math Buddy reads the page and gives hints, then stops. It already knows which school unit each problem is (specFromQuestion, unitOf) and can write six code-checked questions on it with no model call. Put that on the Hint screen: on a school-unit problem the dead 'No lesson for this' pill becomes 'Six like this', and one press turns tonight's homework into a practice set that reaches the ruler.

## Description
The family's most common reason to open Math Buddy is the first door, I have homework. Today that road ends at two hints: the record gets a 'N problems read' line, the ruler never moves, and if the child wants to practise what tripped them up they must leave, open Teach me something, and find on a 15-topic ruler a unit they cannot name - a blind decision the desk already has the answer to. On every school-unit task the Hint screen's second pill is disabled (no lesson library covers the units), so the one action slot beside the hint is wasted exactly where the desk could help most.

The move: kinds.ts gains likeTopic(text, path), pure: the unit a printed task reads as, only when that unit has a code generator and is on the learner's own path. The Hint screen's second stop on such a task is 'Six like this' (Lamplight pill, six icon); Select asks for a set on that unit through the existing set() call with stay, so the hint stays on screen while the six are written ('Writing six like it'), then the Practice paper opens at the learner's own baseline mix (rules/stretch, read by the practice route). The Page side card's kicker names the unit beside the number, so the child knows what kind of problem it is before asking. Nothing new is said on the TV beyond a pill label and a kicker, nothing asks for typing, no answer moves: the six are new questions, written and checked by code.

## Flow
- Page: 'Number 3 · Add and subtract fractions' -> Select -> Hint 1 on the taped card.
- Right -> 'Six like this' -> Select -> topic.open {stay} + /api/practice -> 'Writing six like it' -> practice.set -> the paper with six fractions questions.
- Work them, snap or type -> the Sheet -> the unit's groove on the ruler moves: homework night is on the record.
- A linear or Calculus task keeps today's pills unchanged.

## Expected impact
Five presses plus a blind walk of up to 14 ruler stops become two presses with the unit named by code; a dead pill on every school-unit task becomes the most useful next step; and the homework road, the one families use most, finally feeds the learner's record and the ruler the parent looks at.

## Evaluation
Claim: a homework problem that reads as a school unit on the learner's path can be practised in one press from its hint, and the set reaches the record.
Before: 0 of 6 behaviour cases pass (case 3 is a declared GUARD); the second hint stop is disabled on every school-unit task.
After: 6 of 6 and the guard green; school-marking (test 7 'No lesson for this' route behaviour), tv-keys, maths-tv, maths-type suites unchanged and green.
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: direction (practising a homework problem's unit from its hint is not named in the context map or DESIGN-MATH-BUDDY.md; inside the module's scope, and it is the 'prepare a practice set' leg of the owner's Phase 2 Math change in FAMILY-PHASE-1-PLAN.md section e). No contract change: no route, event or persisted shape moves. Touches the hot shared file desk/src/tv/keys.ts (the hint handler only); avoids store.ts and screens.tsx (screens.tsx:157 keeps HINT_STOPS for the On Air hint).
evidence: api/hint/route.ts:51 `const noLibrary = page.subject === "maths" && (path === "calc1" || kindOfQuestion(item.text) === "school");` MathsTV.tsx:937 `label={s.lesson ? "Show me the lesson" : pickFailed !== null ? "No lesson this time" : s.noLesson ? "No lesson for this" : "Finding the lesson…"} ... disabled={!s.lesson}`. keys.ts:316 `if (at === "lesson" && s.lesson) o.nav("lesson");`. school.ts:2926-2942 unitOf returns one of the 12 generator unit ids (frac-of-amount, frac-equivalent, dec-convert, pct-of-amount, pct-change, ratio-share, unit-rate, area, mean-range, dec-arith, frac-add-sub, frac-mul-div). hint.ts:87 `const unit = spec.school ? topicIn(unitOf(spec.school) ?? "")?.name : undefined;`. api/read/route.ts:30-34 writes only `detail: N problem(s) read`. tools/school-marking-test.cjs:246 pins the no-lesson route behaviour, not the TV label. keys.ts:180-184 set() pushes /api/practice {topic} and topic.open {stay}; store.ts:533 topic.open with stay breaks before changing the screen.

title: Code decides what counts as the child's own words: credit leaves the prompt
body:
## Summary
Every step of a Linga learner's progress, and the certificate a parent is shown, rests on two judgements the model makes in prose: whether a reply demonstrated a skill, and whether it was helped. The rules that keep 'Yes, thank you' and a reply read back from the partner's own line from counting are written in the prompt and nowhere in code. Move them into a small, tested credit table so the stepping stones and the plate mean the child's own English, whatever engine answers.

## Description
The seam: rules.ts validateObservations is the only gate between a model observation and the learner record, and it proves only that the quote is a real substring of the reply (rules.ts:61-64). The three rules that decide credit sit in conversation.ts:214 as instructions, and the support flag that separates 'With help' from 'On your own' is the model's own supportProvided (conversation.ts:59, taken as truth at :229). Downstream, two unsupported successes make a skill 'On your own' (rules.ts:50) and a certificate is issued from those (cert.ts:115-131). Repair is offered on every turn (conversation.ts:221) and required by all six bands (cert.ts:38-53), so the one skill every certificate needs is awarded on model say-so in every scene.

The move is one pure module, credit.ts, with creditOf(quote, skill, shown) -> 'none' | 'helped' | 'own':
- none: the quote is only formula words (yes, no, ok, thanks, thank you, hello, hi, bye, sure, fine, great, cool), or a skill-shape rule fails. Shapes are a short table: repair needs a question mark or a clarifying marker (again, repeat, mean, slowly, sorry, pardon, say, spell, understand; bare wh-words (what, which, where, how) are not repair markers on their own), because spoken transcripts carry no punctuation; request needs a request marker (can, could, would, please, need, want, like, may, '?'); the other skills need at least three words. A teacher can widen the table; it is data.
- helped: the quote repeats four or more consecutive words of something this scene already showed (review.ts's own list: partner lines, the cue, moments, the coach's after), or the whole of a quote under four words appears there.
- own: everything else.
validateObservations applies it: none drops the observation, helped stores it with supported:true. conversation.ts also marks the reply supported when it copies the last partner line, ORed with the model's flag, so code can add support but never remove it. The prompt keeps its sentences; code is now the backstop.

Withholding is untouched: nothing new reaches a screen. No live model call: every case stubs engine.text as tools/linga-rules-test.cjs does.

## Flow
- The child replies; the model returns its observations as today.
- validateObservations runs the existing ten checks, then creditOf against the scene's shown lines.
- A formula or a wrong-shaped repair is dropped; a read-back line is stored as with help; the child's own words are stored as today.
- Progress, the map, the plate's quote and the certificate read the same record and need no change.

## Expected impact
The certificate a parent opens, and the stones on the TV, can no longer be reached by 'Yes, thank you' twice or by reading Pip's line back, on any engine. The plate's quote (cert.ts evidenceFor) is always a line the child built. Before: 3 credit rules and the support rule are prompt-only, 0 enforced in code. After: all four in one table with a suite.

## Evaluation
Claim: credit for a skill is decided in code from the quote and what the scene showed, not by the model's prose compliance.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass as written (cases 1-6 fail: the formula, copied and wrong-shaped quotes are stored as unsupported successes; case 7 is a guard and is green).
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
conversation.ts:214 const credit=" An observation's success is true only when the quoted words themselves do what that skill describes (repair means asking to repeat, clarify or confirm meaning). A thanks, a yes, a single repeated word or a copy of your own words demonstrates no skill: make no observation for it."
conversation.ts:229 supported:moment?true:result.json.supportProvided!==false
conversation.ts:221 validateObservations(result.json.observations,{...,supported:c.supported,text:reply,skills:[...new Set([c.focusSkill,c.reviewSkill??"repair","repair"])]})

Prior decks/findings: no card or finding on credit rules or supportProvided (titles read in 3 decks, 7 findings.jsonl, 4 outbox findings).

title: Every scene is a mission: steps lit on the TV as the child reaches them
body:
## Summary
A Linga scene has a goal and no way to reach it. The child talks to Pip about the lost rover, the TV shows the same goal sentence from the first line to the last, and the scene ends only when someone presses Finish or hits the 24-reply wall. Give every scene two or three steps, light them on the TV as the child's own replies reach them, and let the scene end in 'Mission done' instead of a menu choice. The parent on the sofa, who may not follow the English, can follow the dots.

## Description
Today: EnglishScene and Conversation carry one goal string and nothing about accomplishment (types.ts:19-23, 112-129); the goal is static text under the partner's line (view.ts:429); progressDots is null in a conversation (view.ts:550-562). The design asked for exactly this: 'The scene changes when the learner achieves something' (LINGA-CONVERSATION-DESIGN.md:52) and 'success opportunities' in the contract (:113).

The move:
- mission.ts (pure): missionOf(scene, generated) takes the scene's authored steps, else validated steps from the opening call (2-3 steps, each at most 48 characters), else null. applyStep(mission, claim, reply, turnId) accepts a claim only for the current step, only when its quote is a substring of the reply of at least two words, one step per reply. currentStep and missionDone read it.
- curriculum.ts: three authored steps on each of the 11 built-in scenes, phrased as goals, never as words to say (rover: 'Find out where Pip saw it', 'Ask which way to go', 'Say what you see').
- conversation.ts: the opening schema asks for steps only when the scene has none; the turn schema gains an optional step claim, parsed loosely like the moment, so a bad claim never costs the turn; the context carries currentStep only, never the later steps.
- view.ts: progressDots gives the mission's dots on the talk, moment, coach and recap screens; the scene hero's data line names the current step; when the mission is done the primary action is Finish labelled 'See what you did' and the caption says 'Mission done. See what you did tonight.'; the recap's dots show how far the scene went. viewText prints the mission line for the LT driver.
- LingaTV.tsx: the data line's key reads 'Now' instead of 'Goal'; dots are already drawn. LingaPhone.tsx: the status line under the title names the current step.

Repo law: the model proposes, code decides (exact quote, order, one per reply); a step never writes evidence, so progress and the certificate are untouched; no new screen, no restyle, no typing on the TV; withholding is pinned by case 7; the Topics screen is not touched. No store.ts, screens.tsx or keys.ts edit: mission rides inside Conversation, which linga.changed already carries whole.

Contract: Conversation (session JSON) gains optional mission; the opening and turn schemas gain optional fields. Consumers: view.ts, LingaTV.tsx, LingaPhone.tsx, LingaTestBar.tsx (reads lingaView, unchanged), store.ts load (spreads the conversation, unchanged), the uat driver via viewText and VIEW_ACTION_IDS (no new id: 'finish' is reused), tools/linga-ui-test.cjs (unchanged steps). Inside the module's scope: named in LINGA-CONVERSATION-DESIGN.md:52,113; not the LATER 'collection of places visited', which is across sessions.

## Flow
- Start talking: the TV shows Pip's opening, the footer shows three dots, the data line reads 'Now · Find out where Pip saw it'.
- The child asks 'Where did you see it last?': the model claims step 1 with that quote, code accepts, the first dot fills, the data line moves to step 2.
- After step 3 the primary action becomes 'See what you did'; the child can keep talking or press it.
- The recap's footer shows the filled dots beside tonight's comparison picture.

## Expected impact
The scene becomes a little adventure with a visible end: the child knows how far they are, the parent sees progress as a picture without reading English, and a rehearsal ends because something was achieved. Before: 0 of 11 scenes have steps, 0 conversation screens show progress, 2 ways to end (Finish, the 24-reply wall). After: 11 of 11 authored, every generated topic gets validated steps or none, a third ending: the mission done.

## Evaluation
Claim: each scene carries code-checked steps that light on the TV as the child's own replies reach them, and a finished mission leads to the recap in one press.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass as written (cases 1-7 fail: no mission field, no dots in a conversation, no step claim; case 8 is a guard and is green).
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: types.ts:19-23 export interface EnglishScene { id; name; goal; partner; skill; audience; minutes; premise; cue; quiz } -> no steps curriculum.ts:23 { id: "rover", name: "The missing moon rover", goal: "Find the rover by asking for clues.", ... } -> 11 scenes (lines 17-49), one goal each conversation.ts:198 if(c.turns.filter(t=>t.role==="learner").length>=24&&action==="turn")throw new ConversationError("A good place to pause. Finish this rehearsal and start a new scene.") conversation.ts:195 commit({...c,phase:"finished",...},"linga-recap") -> only on action==='finish' view.ts:429 hero = { kind: "scene", kicker: ..., title: c.goal, who: c.partner, said, subtitle: said ? c.goal : "", ... } view.ts:554-561 progressDots: dots for the check (about/tasks) and home's plan topics; otherwise return null LingaTV.tsx:118 {dots&&} LingaTV.tsx:166 {goal&&Goal{goal}} grep -rn 'steps|milestone|success opportun|achieved|mission' desk/src/lib/english desk/src/english -> no mission state (only art labels and 'Your mission' caption tag, view.ts:232) LINGA-CONVERSATION-DESIGN.md:52 '| Conversation | The scene changes when the learner achieves something |' Prior decks (36 cards) and findings: no card on scene steps or a scene's end; FAMILY-PHASE-1-PLAN.md:47 rejects only the parent walk-on part, not touched here.

title: The model observes, code rules: every essay verdict decided in rules/essay
body:
## Summary
Essay Master's verdicts - which sentence is faulty, whether a rewrite holds, whether a lens goes Secure - are decided by the model in a prompt. Move the decision into rules/essay: the model reports what it sees per sentence (the job it does, the side it takes, the support it gives, a quoted issue), and a pure decideVerdicts() turns those observations, cross-checked against the text, into strong/faulty/neutral.

## Description
The seam: lib/desk/essay.ts:21 and :46 ask the model for the verdict itself, and :60-64 take it as returned. Twelve downstream sites read it (where the page opens, which arrow points back, the specimen card, the landing rail, the 'holds' ink, Next-sentence focus) and three records are written from its count (history, the lens estimate and Secure seal, the weekly digest). Repo law (.claude/spark/config.md:39-41) names exactly this - a sentence role and a mastery verdict in a prompt - as a deviation. The fix follows Linga's in-tree pattern (conversation.ts:221): the schema asks per lens for an observation (structure: job claim|evidence|link|context|none; argument: side pushes|against|wanders|neutral and turnsBack; evidence: support checkable|opinion|context; language: issues [{kind, word}]), plus the note and optional fix as today. rules/essay.decideVerdicts(lens, sentences, observations) decides, with code checks the model cannot talk past: a turn needs a contrast connector in the sentence; 'checkable' needs an EVIDENCE marker or a number to be strong; a vague or repeated word must actually be in the sentence; length is counted by code. A rewrite runs through the same function with the other sentences' first-pass roles as context, so 'holds' means the check that failed now passes. Notes stay the model's words; when code rules faulty and the note is empty, the caption gets the check's own line from rules/essay.

## Flow
- Phone sends a paragraph; splitSentences numbers it (unchanged)
- The model returns observations and notes, no verdict
- decideVerdicts drops observations for missing sentences, verifies quotes and connectors, decides each verdict
- cleanFix keeps a fix only on a code-faulty sentence (unchanged rule)
- history, recordWriting and the digest count code's faulty sentences
- A rewrite: same observation schema for sentence n, same decideVerdicts, so ink follows a rule

## Expected impact
For the family: the Secure seal and the lens ink on the home stop being one model call's opinion; a rewrite inks only when the rule it broke is met, and the caption can say which rule. It unlocks the parked idea that a rewrite that holds may move the lens (the 10-05 rider's open question), because 'holds' becomes a code fact. Engineering: the verdict gets its first unit tests independent of a model; a provider swap (claude to codex to Ollama) can no longer silently change which sentences are faulty.

## Evaluation
Claim: every essay verdict and the rewrite's 'holds' are decided by rules/essay from verified observations, and the records count those verdicts.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (7 fail, the GUARD passes by design); 12 downstream readers and 3 learner-record writes sit on a model-decided enum
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first in tools/essay-rules-test.cjs (engine.text stubbed, no live call)
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
